questions.prompt: What is the fundamental difference between what the $MFT records and what the USN journal records?
options: They record identical data in different formats
The MFT records a file's current state, while the journal records the events that happened to it -- append-only and never edited
The MFT covers system files and the journal covers user files
questions.explanation: Because the journal is an append-only event log, an entry describing a change survives even if the MFT record it referenced is later rewritten or reused.

questions.prompt: Which USN reason code is generated when $SI timestamps are modified?
questions.explanation: Metadata changes including $SI timestamp modification generate BASIC_INFO_CHANGE, recorded at the real time it occurred -- which is what makes the journal a timestomping corroboration source.

questions.prompt: Why must the USN journal be collected early in an engagement?
options: It is deleted automatically after 24 hours
It is a fixed-size circular buffer that wraps, sometimes retaining only days of history on a busy volume
It can only be read while the system is running
It is encrypted after the first reboot
questions.explanation: The journal trades breadth for depth -- enormous event detail over a short window -- so waiting until scoping is complete risks the relevant entries having already wrapped.
